title: Aggregate Accuracy Hides Diagnosis-Specific Failure in Medical Vision-Language Models
summary: On 6,048 balanced ChestX-ray14 cases, HuatuoGPT-Vision and Qwen2.5-VL detected none of 432 pneumothorax-positive cases; comparison models detected 38% and 67%. This model-specific failure also appeared at larger model scale. The failure replicated on an independent SIIM-ACR set with radiologist-drawn masks: the same models detected 0/432 confirmed pneumothoraces, including 0/144 largest lesions. Retrospective diagnostic evaluation only; no clinical benefit established.
ai_technology: Medical vision-language models directly answered per-finding questions from chest radiographs; the study evaluated their diagnosis-specific recall, confidence and internal representations.

source_review.scope: Read the primary preprint Methods and Results; its v1 record dates the result to 11 November 2026. The study directly evaluates medical VLMs on a specific diagnostic question: two models missed every pneumothorax in a balanced ChestX-ray14 audit while other models detected a substantial share; the failure replicated on an independent SIIM-ACR set with radiologist masks. Exact title/result comparison found no matching entry in either supplied catalog. This is retrospective diagnostic validation, not evidence of clinical benefit; ChestX-ray14 labels and binary prompts limit interpretation.
